stem.text: The bacterium Escherichia coli uses glucose as the main respiratory substrate, but other substances, such as lactose, can be used when necessary.
The enzyme β-galactosidase hydrolyses lactose to form glucose and galactose, which can then be used by E. coli.
Production of β-galactosidase in E. coli is regulated and involves a length of DNA known as the lac operon.
Figure 1.1 is a simple diagram of the lac operon.

stem.caption: Figure 1.1
stem.alt: Simple lac operon diagram showing P, O, lacZ, lacY and lacA.

stem.text: When lactose is absent, a repressor molecule is attached to part of the lac operon.
Draw a cross (X) on Figure 1.1 to show the location where the repressor attaches to the lac operon when lactose is absent.

explanation.text: The repressor prevents transcription by binding the operator, rather than a structural gene or the promoter. The operator is the control site labelled O.

reasoningChain: Locate O on the operon diagram.
Place the cross on that control region.

explanation.text: lacY encodes the membrane protein that increases lactose uptake. lacA encodes transacetylase, whose chemical modification role differs from lactose hydrolysis by β-galactosidase.

stem.text: The enzyme β-galactosidase is an inducible enzyme.
Explain what is meant by an inducible enzyme.

points.text: (enzyme that is only) produced when, the substrate / lactose / inducer, is present ; A in larger amounts

explanation.text: An inducible enzyme is produced in response to an inducer rather than being produced continuously at the same level. In this context, lactose availability permits expression of the relevant structural genes.

reasoningChain: Define production in response to an inducer.
Keep the definition about enzyme synthesis rather than activation of pre-existing enzyme.

stem.text: A scientist investigated population growth in E. coli.

items: A sample of E. coli was removed from a liquid nutrient medium containing glucose.
The sample was added to a liquid nutrient medium containing limited quantities of glucose and lactose.
Estimates of the total number of cells in the sample (population size) were made at regular intervals.
